result.title: TAD: Distilling Vision-Language-Action Policies from Teacher Trajectories Alone
result.summary: Online distillation of vision-language-action (VLA) policies commonly relies on teacher action scores that an inference-only interface may not expose. Trajectory-only Adversarial Distillation (\gad{}) instead turns a fixed bank of teacher joint-position features into adaptive feedback: a discriminator compares feature marginals from teacher and student rollouts and supplies rewards for on-policy learning. The student interacts with the environment without online teacher queries or environment task rewards. On ManiSkill \texttt{PutOnPlateInScene25Main}, \gad{} improves OpenVLA-OFT (7B) from $26.2\%$ to $76.6\%$ \successonce{} ($+50.4$ percentage points) and from $20.3\%$ to $58.6\%$ \successend{}. It trails white-box on-policy distillation (OPD) at $81.6\%$ / $59.4\%$ by $5.0$ / $0.8$ percentage points ($n{=}256$ evaluation trajectories per checkpoint). The tested four-epoch continuation achieves the highest \gad{} result without additional teacher data. This best run uses $5\times$ OPD's student interaction budget and $12.5\times$ its complete-rollout batch-passes. The comparison demonstrates online VLA improvement without teacher scoring while quantifying unequal interaction and optimization budgets.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 TAD：用固定的教师 joint-position 轨迹特征库训练判别器，区分教师与学生 rollout 的特征边缘分布并转化为奖励，从而在不查询教师动作分数、不使用环境任务奖励的情况下做 on-policy VLA 策略蒸馏，并在 ManiSkill 上量化其与白盒 OPD 的成功率及交互预算差异。
AI.relevance_reason: 以内部特征分布判别器生成隐式奖励的思路，可能为 LVR 中缺少逐步监督时的轨迹级信用分配与 latent 状态监督提供可核查线索，但研究对象是机器人动作策略而非视觉推理状态，联系需较多验证。
